clue.text: Alliance runs into trouble with gangster

indicators.note: the runs go into the word for trouble, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to trouble someone is to bother them; bother is also a noun meaning trouble
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
a hood (short for hoodlum) is a gangster

explanation.surface: A criminal alliance hits trouble because of a gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: A brotherhood is an association or fellowship of people joined in a common cause, a kind of alliance.

clue.text: Finished term at university with no money to go on

indicators.note: the university piece is placed on top of, i.e. after, the money piece

parts.note: being broke means having no money
UP means at university, as in being up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student finishes the term at university penniless, with nothing to live on.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools and universities a term is said to break up when it ends for the holidays.

clue.text: Homer's last letter — so ultimately fantastic

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word so

parts.note: mega is slang for fantastic or great

explanation.surface: A remark that the final letter written by Homer is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: Homer wrote in Greek, so his alphabet ends with this letter; the surface makes it sound like the poet's last letter to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, the one Homer would have used.

clue.text: The opportunity to understand sense supporting deer

indicators.note: in a down clue the sense piece sits below the deer piece, holding it up

parts.note: a hind is a female deer
sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: A puzzling claim that a sense propping up a deer offers a chance to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindsight is understanding an event only after it has happened, the chance to grasp it looking back.

clue.text: Capital equipment on the west of America

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment, as in a drilling rig

indicators.note: the west of a word written left to right is its first letter

explanation.surface: Capital equipment, i.e. heavy investment goods, installed on America's west coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital equipment' reads as a business phrase, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Riga is the capital city of Latvia.

clue.text: Conventional old hot rod smashed times

indicators.note: a smashed hot rod has its letters broken and rearranged

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: An old hot rod car crashed several times, which is hardly conventional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'times' reads as part of the crash story, but it is the multiplication sign; 'smashed' covers only the hot rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthodox means following accepted, traditional or established beliefs and practice.

clue.text: Avoid sharp practice

definitions.meaning: a dishonest trick or swindle, as in a tax wheeze

explanation.surface: Advice to steer clear of underhand dealing.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to evade; as a noun it is a cunning or shady scheme.

clue.text: Fund-raiser making tabloid sound feeble

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging term for a low-quality newspaper such as a tabloid

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for feeble is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: weak means feeble

explanation.surface: A charity effort that makes a tabloid newspaper seem feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: RAG WEEK is a British university tradition: a week of student stunts raising money for charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag week is the annual student charity drive, so it is a fund-raising event.

clue.text: Very taken by new air base — that's irritating

indicators.note: the very piece is taken into, and held inside, the rearranged letters
new signals the air base letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Someone finds a newly built air base deeply irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges AIRBASE to ABRASIE, with V going in before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasive literally means scraping or grating, and figuratively describes a harsh, annoying manner.

clue.text: Quickly finished thing needing adjustment

parts.note: over means finished, as in the game is over

indicators.note: the word thing needs its letters adjusted into a new order

explanation.surface: Something done in a hurry that now needs fixing.
explanation.definitionFit: Overnight can mean suddenly or very rapidly, as in an overnight success.

clue.text: First appearance cut short — good. Remove errors from programme

indicators.note: cut short tells us to lop off the final letter of the word

parts.note: a debut is a first appearance on stage or in a team

explanation.surface: A debut ended early, which was good, and a programme needs its glitches fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes T off DEBUT, leaving DEBU.
explanation.definitionFit: To debug software is to find and fix the faults in its code.

clue.text: Pass, as error by East

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for East
a lapse is a slip or error

explanation.surface: A sporting pass counted as a mistake by the player out East.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to elapse when it passes or goes by.

clue.text: Monitor avoiding extremes

definitions.meaning: to oversee and control a discussion or exam marking, as a verb
middle-of-the-road, not excessive, as an adjective

explanation.surface: A supervisor who keeps away from anything extreme.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to supervise a forum; as an adjective it means temperate and restrained.

clue.text: Soup tureen with a covering of glaze

parts.note: a tureen is a deep pot for serving soup

indicators.note: the covering of a word is its outside, here its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Soup served in a tureen that has a glazed finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Potage is a thick soup, the French word used in English cookery.

clue.text: Go after poor act I, saying little

indicators.note: after puts the go piece behind the rearranged letters
a poor act gets its letters rearranged into a better shape

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in it is your turn

explanation.surface: An actor going on after a weak first act with hardly any lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A taciturn person is reserved and uncommunicative, speaking very little.

clue.text: Air traffic controller's delight with son getting credit

parts.note: joy is delight
on tick means on credit, so tick is credit

explanation.surface: An air traffic controller is pleased that their son has got a loan.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition means a controller of air traffic, the pilot's control lever, not the person in the tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A joystick is the control lever a pilot uses to steer an aircraft through the air.

clue.text: Fight on beer wagon up where they recycle

parts.note: a scrap is a fight

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a dray is a low cart used for delivering beer barrels

explanation.surface: A brawl breaks out on a brewer's cart at the recycling centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapyard is a site where scrap metal and old vehicles are collected for reuse.

clue.text: Pleasure-seeking housewife disheartened — academic is married!

indicators.note: with its heart removed only the outer letters of housewife survive

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A dispirited housewife exclaims that the academic is married.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonism is the pursuit of pleasure as the chief aim of life, i.e. pleasure-seeking as a noun.

clue.text: Subtleties of French resort with connections

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
ties are connections or links

explanation.surface: The fine points of a Riviera resort with good links.
explanation.definitionFit: Niceties are fine distinctions or details, the subtle points of something.

clue.text: Innocently and strangely alive in the Big Apple

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go in between the city's two letters

parts.note: the Big Apple is a nickname for New York, NY

indicators.note: strangely signals the letters of alive arranged oddly

explanation.surface: Someone wanders New York, innocent and oddly full of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' scrambles the letters of alive, which then sit between the city's two initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Naively means in an innocent, unsophisticated, trusting way.

clue.text: Welcomes political activists having time for North

indicators.note: having time for North means the time letter replaces the North letter

parts.note: the Greens are environmental political activists
N is the compass abbreviation for North

explanation.surface: Environmental campaigners welcome a stint up North.
explanation.definitionFit: To greet someone is to welcome them on arrival.

clue.text: Yes — worried about call for needle!

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, i.e. around, the call piece
worried signals the letters of yes are disturbed

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them

explanation.surface: Someone agrees, anxious about the injection call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' scrambles yes, and the call sits after its first two scrambled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypodermic syringe is fitted with a needle, and the word is used for the whole device.

clue.text: Engineer on metric telephone system

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or build, so the letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: An engineer works on a metric phone network.
explanation.definitionFit: An intercom is an internal communication system, a kind of telephone link within a building.

clue.text: They're licensed to store a bit of the past

indicators.note: the licensed people store the letters inside their words, spanning both

explanation.surface: Licensed traders keep an antique in stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object surviving from an earlier time, a fragment of history.

clue.text: Spinner's pride broken after first of sixes

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters behind the opening letter
first of picks the opening letter of sixes
broken pride has its letters scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A cricket spin bowler's pride is hurt after being hit for sixes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges PRIDE to PIDER. The cricket surface makes 'Spinner' a spin bowler; it is the web-spinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider spins silk to make webs, so it is a natural spinner.

clue.text: Desiccant that is right — under the doctor!

indicators.note: in a down clue the later pieces sit under the doctor piece

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
IE (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: A drying agent prescribed correctly by the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A drier is a substance that absorbs moisture or speeds drying, as a desiccant does.

clue.text: Source of iron in the majority of cereal fibre

indicators.note: the iron letter goes in the shortened cereal
the majority of a four-letter word is its first three, so the last letter goes

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Breakfast cereal fibre that contains plenty of iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the majority of' cuts CORN to COR.
explanation.definitionFit: Coir is the coarse fibre from coconut husks, used for matting and rope.

clue.text: Register as retired single, keeping married at heart

indicators.note: the reversed word keeps the middle letter held inside it
retired means drawn back, so the word for single is read backwards

parts.note: lone means single or solitary

indicators.note: at heart points to the central letter of married

explanation.surface: A retired single person keeps marriage close to their heart when signing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns LONE into ENOL, and R goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to register or enter one's name on a list or course.

clue.text: Sit in a loo, uneasily, in solitude

indicators.note: uneasily suggests the letters sit restlessly and shift around

explanation.surface: Someone sits uncomfortably on the toilet, alone with their thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolation is the state of being alone or apart from others, which solitude also describes.

clue.text: Appeared to accept a troubled raider's friendship

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: came means appeared or arrived

indicators.note: troubled signals the letters of raider are disturbed

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter, leaving just the word raider as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone seemed to accept the friendship of a troubled bandit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appeared' is a past tense, so its synonym is came, which opens up to hold everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Camaraderie is mutual trust and comradeship among people who spend time together.
